drv_pdm_buffer_get_resolution.root_cause: the differing word is the base address of the driver-owned static scratch buffer pdm_pcm_block (drv_pdm.c:95, `static uint8_t pdm_pcm_block[320]`, comment 'stock RAM 0x2006fc4c'). Stock fixes it at 0x2006fc4c (literal [0x57ba84]); the C's static linked into harness .bss elsewhere, so *buffer returned a different (equally valid) address. NOT a logic bug: both bodies read the identical raw DMA buffer (run-stock am_hal_pdm_dma_get_buffer 0x59262c) and apply the identical 23..8/23..16 byte extraction.
drv_pdm_buffer_get_resolution.proof: bound the C static to the stock address via harness-only linker section placement (place_pdm.ld: .bss.pdm_pcm_block @0x2006fc4c; nm confirms pdm_pcm_block=0x2006fc4c). With both buffers co-located, all 6 seeds match fully (pointer + 320-byte PCM contents + length). Proven harness binding artifact; resolved; NO firmware edit.
drv_pdm_buffer_get_resolution.classification: harness artifact (static internal-scratch link address), PROVEN, resolved

preinit_note: PREINIT['pdm']=('DRV_PdmInit',0x20071000,0x4000) runs the real DRV_PdmInit once before snapshot (instance table 0x200718c8 + handle cell 0x2007454c + init flag 0x20074fba all within the 0x4000 snap window), restored identically for both variants. Ran in Renode with NO hang on unmodeled PDM hardware (am_hal_pdm_dma_start is a pure descriptor->handle struct copy; register writes are ignored by Renode).
